text: In the lac/lacUV5 inducible promoter system, how does IPTG induce gene expression?
choices: IPTG is metabolized into allolactose, which is the only molecule capable of binding and inactivating LacI
IPTG binds directly to the -10 promoter element, physically recruiting RNA polymerase
IPTG binds the LacI repressor, causing a conformational change that reduces LacI-DNA affinity roughly 1000-fold and releases the repressor from the operator
IPTG activates AraC, which then binds the I1 and I2 sites to activate the promoter
explanation: IPTG binds LacI directly and triggers a conformational change that drops its DNA-binding affinity approximately 1000-fold, releasing LacI from the operator and permitting transcription. IPTG is valued as a research tool precisely because it is not metabolized (choice 0 is incorrect) -- it is a synthetic, non-metabolizable analog of the natural inducer allolactose, not a precursor to it. Choice 1 misattributes the mechanism to direct promoter binding rather than repressor inactivation, and choice 3 describes an entirely different system (arabinose/AraC), not the lac system.
